question: How and why did this happen here, in its real setting?

crowe2011.cite: Crowe et al. (2011). The case study approach. BMC Medical Research Methodology 11: 100.
crowe2011.checked: every quote read word for word in the text copy of the published PDF in the user's research library (No. 286) on 20 Nov 2026; places are the article's page numbers (p. N of 9) and section headings; in-text reference numbers are left out of the quotes

steps.title: Define the case
steps.text: Say what the case is and where it stops: which organisation or group, which period, which evidence. The boundary decides what counts as data.

quotes.text: each case should have a pre-defined boundary which clarifies the nature and time period covered by the case study

steps.title: Select the case
steps.text: Pick the case for what it can teach: a unique case for its own sake, or typical cases that let you test a theory again in a second or third case.

quotes.text: The case is selected not because it is representative of other cases, but because of its uniqueness, which is of genuine interest to the researchers.
quotes.where: p. 5, “Selecting the case(s)”, on intrinsic case studies

quotes.text: to test theory by replicating the findings in a second or even a third case (i.e. replication logic)

steps.title: Collect many sources
steps.text: Gather several kinds of evidence about the same case (documents, interviews, observation, routine numbers) and see whether they agree.

quotes.text: The use of multiple sources of data (data triangulation) has been advocated as a way of increasing the internal validity of a study

steps.title: Within, then across
steps.text: Describe and code each case on its own first. Only then set the cases side by side to see what they share and where they differ.

quotes.text: In collective case studies, it is helpful to analyse data relating to the individual component cases first, before making comparisons across cases.
quotes.where: p. 7, “Analysing, interpreting and reporting case studies”

steps.title: Generalise to theory
steps.text: A case speaks to a theory, not to a population. Use theory to explain the case, without bending the case to fit it.

quotes.text: allow theoretical (as opposed to statistical) generalisation beyond the particular cases studied
quotes.where: p. 7, “Analysing, interpreting and reporting case studies”

quotes.text: the cases should not be “forced to fit” the particular theoretical framework that is being employed.

external-validity.text: Case study research has sometimes been criticised for lacking scientific rigour and providing little basis for generalisation

limits: One source only: Crowe et al. (2011), the card's own reference. Yin's and Stake's textbooks, which Crowe et al. build on, were not read.
